confirmed.claim: qualiNetDone is never cleared when a friend-race qualifying is abandoned, so every later qualifying session in the same page load is soft-locked behind a permanently disabled TO THE GRID button.
confirmed.evidence: The only sites touching qualiNetDone are its declaration (756), openQualiForNet (811, sets it), and the $("q-go") handler (7309-7311, the sole clear). quitToMenu (2904-2938) clears quali.clear() and qualiPeers.clear() but not qualiNetDone; openQuali (7268-7281) likewise; lobby teardown (js/net/lobby.js:259) cannot reach this closure. With a stale qualiNetDone, qualiNetWaiting() (757-766) runs: netPlay.rivalDriverIds() is [] after session teardown (netplay.js:749 maps remoteList(), emptied at 375-377), so it falls to `return !(qualiPeers.size > 0)` — qualiPeers was cleared, so waiting=true, q-go is disabled reading "WAITING FOR THEIR LAP…" (776-804) with no rival to ever report; and were it pressed, q-go would invoke the dead lobby finishStart instead of closeQualiToGrid.
confirmed.fix: Clear qualiNetDone (and the qualiLive map) in quitToMenu() and at the top of openQuali(), alongside the existing quali.clear()/qualiPeers.clear().

confirmed.claim: coast()'s bare `Math.max(24, c.speed - 20 * dt)` floor RAISES a finished car's speed to 24 m/s and ignores PACE — the exact bare-Math.max floor shape this same file documents as a bug for grass drag.
confirmed.evidence: Line 4656: `c.speed = Math.max(24, c.speed - 20 * dt);`. The grass-drag comment at 3706-3717 explains why that shape is wrong ("The floor used to be a bare Math.max, so any time you were off-track below 10.8 m/s it RAISED your speed") and why such floors must be pace-scaled (`GRASS_V * 0.6 * Math.max(PACE, 0.05)` at 3715). At PACE < ~0.55, vTop() = VMAX*PACE < 24, so a finished car cruises ABOVE the game's top speed; a car crossing the line below 24 m/s is instantly accelerated to 24. Invisible to tools/vstd-lint.mjs (it only matches comparison operators, CMP_NUM at vstd-lint.mjs:102) and absent from the ALLOWED list in tests/unit/vstd-invariant.test.mjs.
confirmed.fix: Scale the floor by pace: `c.speed = Math.min(c.speed, Math.max(24 * Math.max(PACE, 0.05), c.speed - 20 * dt))` or equivalently floor at `24 * Math.max(PACE, 0.05)` without ever raising speed.

confirmed.claim: render() dereferences `player.speed` with player=null on the boot menu whenever LT.speedBlur > 0, killing every subsequent frame (the menu freezes).
confirmed.evidence: The `state === "menu"` branch (5184-5190) builds the flyby camera without a player and falls through; the `if (!player) return;` guard (5192) is inside the else branch only. Line 6518 then runs unconditionally: `const _spd = LT.speedBlur > 0 ? LT.speedBlur * clamp(((player.speed || 0) / vTop() - 0.4) / 0.5, 0, 1) : 0;` — before the first race `player` is null (declared null at 608, first assigned in makeCars). speedBlur defaults to 0 (js/game/lighting.js:262 `def: 0.0`) so normal boot survives, but `__apex.lightTune({speedBlur:0.5})` from the menu makes this throw before gfx.present(6563); tick() (6588-6598) reports once and rethrows every rAF.
confirmed.fix: Use `((player && player.speed) || 0)` at 6518, matching the null-guards the env-probe (5894) and shadow passes (5561, 5803) already carry.

confirmed.claim: launchFlyingLap's inner comment describes launching at the player's own top speed "capped by what the road at the line will actually take", but the code performs no such computation — it sets player.speed = 0.
confirmed.evidence: Lines 2219-2227 read "The player's OWN top speed — the identical expression updateCar() uses … Launching off it would start them a quarter down … Then capped by what the road at the line will actually take, so a circuit whose start/finish sits in a corner does not launch the car into a wall." No speed is computed anywhere in the function; line 2234 is `player.speed = 0;   // standing start, like the real thing`, and the function's own header (2205-2211) says the racing-speed launch was removed. The Tracks.sample at 2228 is also redundant — worldFromTrack(2231) re-samples the same s into smp.
confirmed.fix: Delete the stale 2219-2227 block (the header comment already tells the true story) and drop the redundant Tracks.sample at 2228.

confirmed.claim: G.ACCEL is a facade export nothing consumes — and the comment directly above it explains why no consumer should exist.
confirmed.evidence: Line 2770 exports `LAT_MAX, ACCEL, BRAKE` onto G. Grep across js/ finds zero `G.ACCEL` reads and apex.js's destructure (apex.js:14-19) omits it; quali.js uses G.LAT_MAX, G.BRAKE and G.aTop() (quali.js:95-101). The facade's own comment (2766-2769) says "LAT_MAX and BRAKE … pass through as constants; acceleration goes through aTop()", and the aTop() comment at 327-330 records that quali.js reading `G.ACCEL` was itself the bug aTop() fixed.
confirmed.fix: Remove ACCEL from the G literal at 2770.

confirmed.claim: `hidePlayerCar && !cockpitRigOnly` can never be true, so the player-skip `continue` at the top of the car draw loop is unreachable.
confirmed.evidence: Lines 5935-5939: `hidePlayerCar = !dbgCam && (state==="race"||state==="count") && CAM_MODES[camMode].id === "cockpit"` and `cockpitRigOnly = hidePlayerCar && CAM_MODES[camMode].id === "cockpit"` — the second condition is already implied by the first, so the two booleans are always equal. Line 5952 `if (c.isPlayer && hidePlayerCar && !cockpitRigOnly) continue;` therefore never fires; only the cockpit-rig branch at 6100 is live.
confirmed.fix: Collapse to one boolean (cockpitRigOnly) and delete the dead continue at 5952, or restore the distinction if hood/tcam were meant to hide the body too.

confirmed.claim: resolveCamera's orbit branch hardcodes the synthetic camera's eye/target Y at ~0.6 m absolute, ignoring road elevation, so render({what:'view',orbit:...}) frames from under (or far above) the scene on any circuit with elevation while still returning a plausible-looking raster.
confirmed.evidence: Line 111-113: eye = [p.px + dx*dist*cos(el), 0.6 + dist*sin(el), p.pz + dz*dist*cos(el)]; tgt = [p.px, 0.6, p.pz] — no track Y sample anywhere in the branch. The sibling camVantage branch's own comment (lines 124-129) warns that a mis-derived synthetic eye 'can land hundreds of metres away while the raster still comes back fully populated and plausible-looking', and the equivalent hook apex.js carOrbit (lines 789-802) samples the road and uses smp.p[1] + h for exactly this purpose. On a track section 20 m above datum the orbit eye/target sit ~19 m below the car.
confirmed.fix: Sample Tracks.sample(G.track, p.s, scr) and base both eye and tgt Y on scr.p[1] (e.g. scr.p[1] + 0.6), as carOrbit does.

confirmed.claim: startRain() silently drops the request while a previous stopRain() is still in its 1.2 s teardown window, and because callers only fire on discrete weather flips, rain audio then stays off for the rest of the wet session.
confirmed.evidence: Line 663: `if (!sfxOk() || rainStopping) return;` — stopRain() (683-696) sets rainStopping=true and only clears it in a 1200 ms setTimeout. startRain is only called at race start (game.js:2375) and on weather change (game.js:2959 setWeatherLive), so a rain→dry→rain flip inside 1.2 s (live weather sync, weatherArc, or a quick restart) leaves the rain loop permanently silent with no retry.
confirmed.fix: In startRain, when rainStopping is set, either cancel the pending teardown and re-target the existing gain, or record a pending gain that the stopRain timeout callback starts.

confirmed.claim: reset() syncs only the arc render anchors (rPrevS/rPrevX) and omits the world anchors rPrevPx/rPrevPz, so the first rendered frame after a reset draws the player lerped between the pre-reset and post-reset world positions.
confirmed.evidence: Line 2667: `G.player.rPrevS = G.player.s; G.player.rPrevX = G.player.x;   // sync render anchors (see jump)` — but jump() (lines 129-130) additionally syncs rPrevPx/rPrevPz with a comment explaining the human car is drawn from the WORLD pair, and aiPlace() (line 2463) syncs all four for the same reason. game.js playerAnchor (1071-1072) computes the drawn position as rPrevPx + (px - rPrevPx) * renderAlpha, so a stale rPrevPx after reset() draws the car part-way to its old location until the next step().
confirmed.fix: Add `G.player.rPrevPx = G.player.px; G.player.rPrevPz = G.player.pz;` next to the existing anchor sync in reset().

confirmed.claim: sky() snaps G.camFov to 75 while its own skyViewOverride declares fov 78, contradicting the adjacent comment 'snap immediately so the very first rendered frame is correct' — the first frame renders at a different FOV than every later one.
confirmed.evidence: Line 165 sets `G.skyViewOverride = { eye: e, tgt: t, fov: 78 }`; line 169 sets `G.camFov = 75;`. game.js (5259-5263) feeds skyViewOverride.fov (78) into the eased fovT while frozen, so camFov glides 75→78 after the first frame — the comment at 162 even derives the framing from FOV 78.
confirmed.fix: Set G.camFov = 78 (or read the value from the override object) so the snap matches the override.

confirmed.claim: plan({northUp:true}) keeps egocentric field names and comments — aheadM/rightM on cars and index entries, and bearingDeg documented '0=ahead,+=right' — but in north-up mode rx/rz are world east/north deltas, so 'aheadM' actually means metres north regardless of the car's heading.
confirmed.evidence: Line 675: `const bearing = (rx, rz) => r1(Math.atan2(rx, -rz) * 180 / Math.PI); // 0=ahead,+=right`; entries (line 680) and cars (line 651) emit aheadM: r1(-c.rz), rightM: r1(c.rx). toCell (lines 590-601) only rotates into the car frame when bodyUp is true; in north-up mode rx=dx (east) and rz=dz, yet the field names and the bearing comment still claim the car frame. The scale.note (741-742) is frame-aware but the index fields are not.
confirmed.fix: In north-up mode rename the emitted fields (e.g. northM/eastM) or compute aheadM/rightM/bearingDeg from the car's actual heading.

confirmed.claim: worldModel().spans hand-rolls `sp.side > 0 ? "right" : "left"`, collapsing side 0/null to 'left' — exactly the mistake the module's own sideOf() helper (lines 1455-1460) exists to prevent ('Collapsing both into "left" was wrong twice'), and which describe('span:N') already fixed by calling sideOf.

confirmed.claim: Doc comments are detached from the methods they describe in at least four places: fetchTrackOutline's doc sits ~240 lines above its definition (directly over logs()), the tracks()/trackGraph() docs are stacked above renderClock(), the setEnergy doc sits above setBoost, and the aero() doc sits above aeroMode().

confirmed.claim: The step() idle fast-path omits live B2 barrier panels from its checks, so once queued impacts, shards and marbles drain, the world freezes with panels still live — updatePanels() never runs again, a broken panel is rendered frozen mid-scatter (draw() line 1087 keeps drawing it from its stale Rapier pose), hazards() (line 929) counts a frozen sleeping panel forever, and _panels leaks to PANEL_CAP=10 after which promoteBarrier() returns 0 for the session.

The PANEL_IDLE_DESPAWN_S comment at lines 151-160 documents that unbroken panels leaking permanently 'retired breakable barriers for the rest of the session' — this gate reintroduces that exact leak.

confirmed.claim: The module header describes the baked light records as 'septets' (7 floats) while every record in the file is 15 floats and every consumer strides by 15.

The queued game.js buildStudioRig bug (14-float records misread by the stride-15 pipeline) shows the record length is exactly the detail a maintainer will look up here.

Career.js exports both (hash at career.js:137, rnd at :140), so the header names the wrong, explicitly-rejected API.

confirmed.claim: profile()'s bridge ground window uses wrap01(bridge.s) without adding def._sceneryShift, while buildCenterline raises the deck at (b.s + _sceneryShift), so on any circuit with both bridges and sceneryStartFrac the terrain-stays-flat carve lands ~0.62 of a lap away from the actual deck.
confirmed.evidence: surface.js:65 `const center = TrackSpace.wrap01(bridge.s) * track.total;` vs tracks.js:101-104 `const dress = def._sceneryShift || 0; ... const cs = ((b.s + dress) % 1) * total;`. Measured via tools/track-build-vm.cjs on suzuka (the one shipped def with both, bridges s=0.8173 fmapped, _sceneryShift=0.6198): at the dressed frac 0.4371 (the measured figure-8 self-crossing) ground[k]==py[k]==13.53 (terrain rises with the deck, zero clearance under the crossover), while at the unshifted 0.8173 ground[k]=-2.57 vs py[k]=10.93 — a phantom 13.5 m carve under plain road.
confirmed.fix: In TrackSurface.profile, compute the bridge centre as TrackSpace.wrap01(bridge.s + (def._sceneryShift || 0)) * track.total, matching buildCenterline.

confirmed.claim: The bridge-support pillar pass anchors at Math.round(b.s * n) without def._sceneryShift, so on Suzuka the four pillar pairs stand at racing frac ~0.817 (ordinary road, floating over the spuriously carved trench) while the actual raised crossover at ~0.437 gets no supports.
confirmed.evidence: tracks.js:2272-2273 `if (brs) for (const b of brs) { const kc = Math.round(b.s * n) % n;` with no dress shift, versus buildCenterline tracks.js:104 `const cs = ((b.s + dress) % 1) * total;`. VM build of suzuka: deck bump applied at frac 0.4371 (matches the measured self-crossing 0.4371/0.8458); pillar anchor b.s=0.8173; py[0.8173*n]=10.93 >= 1 so pillars ARE emitted there. docs/tracks/START-LINES.md §4 records the buildCenterline fix but not these two consumers.
confirmed.fix: Use kc = Math.round(TrackSpace.wrap01(b.s + (def._sceneryShift || 0)) * n) % n in the pillar loop (same shift as the deck bump).

confirmed.claim: TrackModels.create().groundPatch is exported but never called (every call site resolves to tracks.js's own groundPatch at line 1116), and if ever wired it would emit at wrong coordinates — its box centre [dist*side, y-h/2, 0] is a track-local lateral offset used as a world position with no origin translation.
confirmed.evidence: Grep for groundPatch across js/: definitions at models.js:207 and tracks.js:1116; tracks.js:2088 and all circuit files bind the tracks.js const; `models.groundPatch` has zero call sites. models.js:218 `const center = [dist * (spec.side || 1), y - spec.size[1] / 2, 0];` is passed straight to box()/emitBox (RAW.addBox) which treats c as world coords.

confirmed.claim: scanBarrier (and indexSolid at 1218) compute k0 = Math.round(s0 * n) % n without wrapping negatives, so a caller passing s0 < 0 (e.g. groundPatch's `recordBarrier(k/n - halfFrac, ...)` when k is near 0, or an authored negative fraction on an untransformed circuit) walks negative typed-array indices: hw[k] reads undefined, the face coords go NaN, and the barrier tighten/segment records for the pre-wrap nodes are silently dropped.
confirmed.evidence: tracks.js:1186 `const k0 = Math.round(s0 * n) % n` then line 1193 `const k = (k0 + i) % n;` with no +n; JS (-2 % 400) === -2. groundPatch at 1141-1143 passes `k / n - halfFrac` which is negative for small k. Contrast waterRaster (line 1029) which wraps with ((a % n) + n) % n. No circuit currently passes opts.collision to groundPatch, so the path is latent.
confirmed.fix: Wrap in scanBarrier/indexSolid: `const k0 = ((Math.round(s0 * n) % n) + n) % n;` (k1 likewise).

[0.45, 0.28, 0.3] : [0.78, 0.42, 0.32];` while nine lines later the same loop's window bands gate on NIGHT (line 1957 `if (NIGHT) {`), and line 427 defines NIGHT = track._night != null ? track._night : !!def.night precisely so buildings 'respond to dusk/night even on a day-default circuit'.

TrackSpace.toRacingFrac/scenerySpace use def.startFrac/def.reverse (space.js:12-14, 60).

confirmed.claim: cameraTower lattice and scaffold legs pass centre-anchored offsets to the BASE-anchored addCyl, so every leg floats h/2-0.4 above ground and overshoots the platform by h/2+0.4.
confirmed.evidence: Line 455: `addCyl(out, vadd(foot, p.u, h / 2 - 0.4), 0.13, h + 0.8, col, 4, b)` (scaffold branch line 447-448 identical idiom). geom.js:196-206 shows addCyl emits from `c` to `c + u*h` (base-anchored: `top = vadd(c, u, h)`), so the legs span y = h/2-0.4 to 3h/2+0.4 while the platform sits at y = h (line 468). The monopole branch in the SAME function uses the correct base idiom (`addFrustum(out, vadd(p.c, p.u, -0.4), ..., h + 0.8, ...)`, line 443), as do bleacher/scaffoldStand legs (lines 623-624, 689). KIT assigns lattice/scaffold camera style to ~30 of 40 circuits, so floating camera-mast legs ship fleet-wide.

confirmed.claim: broadcastCompound's link mast uses the same centre-anchored idiom against base-anchored addCyl, so the mast floats mastH/2-0.4 off the ground and its top overshoots the warning-lamp boxes.

confirmed.claim: grandstandEx pushes tierLift even when the tier's concourse band and crowd were rejected by rejBox, so the roof is lifted 7.6-15.2 m for upper decks that were never built.

confirmed.claim: motorhome's 'slide-out awning canopy' is a 0.05 m-deep box positioned at the posts, so no canopy spans from the unit to the posts the code builds to hold it up.

confirmed.claim: present() dereferences bloomLv[0] unguarded, but createTargets() can leave bloomLv empty with postEnabled still true, crashing every frame with a TypeError.

confirmed.fix: Gate the bloom pass and composite bind on `bloomLv.length > 0` (treat an empty chain like bloomAmt <= 0, binding blackTex).

confirmed.claim: opts.swapYZ swaps Y/Z of positions and normals (a det=-1 reflection) without reversing triangle winding, so a swapYZ-loaded model renders inside-out under GLX's CCW backface culling.
confirmed.evidence: Line 367 `if (swapYZ) p = [p[0], p[2], p[1]];` and line 372 swap the normal the same way; indices are emitted unmodified at line 395 (`idxOut.push(indices[i] + vertBase)`). GLX.init sets `gl.cullFace(gl.BACK); gl.frontFace(gl.CCW)` (glx.js:376-377). Latent: the only shipped callers (game.js:1589, 2011) pass only scale/tint.
confirmed.fix: When swapYZ is set, emit each triangle's indices in reversed order (a,c,b) to restore CCW winding.

confirmed.claim: hdrMode()/hdrOk() reports 'scene buffer is float (HDR)' per the gfx.js contract, but it only tests extension presence — when the post chain fails and rendering goes direct to the 8-bit default framebuffer it still returns true.

confirmed.fix: Make hdrOk() return `postEnabled && colorType === gl.HALF_FLOAT` (envInit's format pick can keep reading colorType directly).

confirmed.claim: TLX drops carShadowBegin's second argument (boxScale), so the car-map depth bias is never scaled when SHADOW DISTANCE widens the car box, breaking the GLX parity the port claims.
confirmed.evidence: tlx.js:802 `carShadowBegin(vp) { if (shadowSys) shadowSys.carShadowBegin(vp); }` and tlx-shadow.js:197 `function carShadowBegin(lightVP)` take one arg, while game.js:5581 calls `gfx.carShadowBegin(_mCVP, cBox / 42)` with cBox = 42*max(1, sBox/80) (game.js:5572). GLX stores it (glx/shadow.js:253 `S.carBoxScale = boxScale || 1`), uploads it as uCarBiasScale (glx.js:991), and lit.js:707 applies `cz = cs.z - biasTerm * uCarBiasScale`; tsl-lit.js:380 uses the unscaled `cs.z.sub(biasTerm)`.
confirmed.fix: Thread boxScale through shadowSys.carShadowBegin into a carBiasScale uniform and multiply biasTerm by it in tsl-lit's car-map compare, mirroring lit.js:707.

confirmed.claim: resize()'s `canvas.clientWidth || canvas.width` fallback feeds the just-set backing-store size back into the DPR multiply, so a zero-clientWidth (hidden/detached) canvas doubles its render size every begin() until GPU allocation fails.
confirmed.evidence: tlx.js:607 `const cw = canvas.clientWidth || canvas.width || 1;` then :610 `const w = Math.max(1, Math.round(cw * dpr * renderScale));` and :614 `renderer.setSize(w, h, false)` which writes canvas.width = w. With clientWidth 0 and DPR_CAP 2, each frame computes w = previous w * 2. GLX and WGX (wgx.js:833) use clientWidth directly with a floor of 1 and cannot loop.
confirmed.fix: Drop the `|| canvas.width` term (use `canvas.clientWidth || 1`), or remember the CSS size separately instead of reading back the buffer size.

confirmed.claim: Eight comments across tlx-post.js and tsl-post.js cite the non-existent path "glx/js/render/shaders/post.js" — a search-and-replace artifact that points maintainers at a file that isn't there.

confirmed.claim: Starting the race never stops the reopened room-code subscription or its pending minted invite transport, so a late joiner on the still-live code corrupts host state mid-race.
confirmed.evidence: finishStart() (919-980) and the quali branch of beginRace() (888-903) end by calling close() (1568-1580), which only clears pollTimer/scan/wake — stopCodeWait() is called only from codeHost/codeJoin/cancel/the vs-close sub-step handler. After a room-code guest connects, onConnected() (418-427) reopens the room via codeHost({quiet:true}), which mints a fresh pending transport and re-subscribes (hostRoom, 1311). Press START and the room, its relay sockets, and the gathering RTCPeerConnection all survive into the race (until the 120 s JOIN_TIMEOUT). A second guest joining mid-race drives onJoiner→acceptAnswer→waitForOpen→onConnected: the lobby's 25 ms pumpTimer restarts alongside NetPlay, a session NetPlay never adopts is created, and openRoom() (535-546) runs G.setNetRoom(true) mid-race — game.js:7028/7238 then routes garage/race-settings exits back to the hidden #vsfriend dialog.
confirmed.fix: In finishStart() (and the quali branch of beginRace()) call stopCodeWait() and dropPending(), and clear codeReopen, before handing the sessions to NetPlay.

confirmed.claim: directExchange() classifies host vs guest by mintOffer/onJoiner, so the two-party host mode its own header and docs/MULTIPLAYER.md teach (send-only, 'resolves when the answer arrives') publishes the invite on the answer topic and silently deadlocks for the full two-minute timeout.
confirmed.evidence: Line 231: `const hosting = !!(mintOffer || onJoiner);` then mineTopic = roomId(code + (hosting ? "|offer" : "|answer")). The exchange contract at lines 93-95 ("host   send: <invite>   resolves when the answer arrives / guest  reply: offer => <answer>") and docs/MULTIPLAYER.md:65 ("The host posts and waits; the guest passes a `reply`") describe a send-only host. Such a caller gets hosting=false: it publishes its invite on the "|answer" topic and listens on "|offer"; the guest (reply set, also hosting=false) also listens on "|offer" — nobody ever publishes there, so both sides wait out JOIN_TIMEOUT_MS. The legacy Trystero branch handles this caller correctly (`else if (send)`, line 733, single shared room). Latent today only because lobby's public-path host always uses hostRoom (onJoiner) and swap-as-host only runs on the private relay — but the documented API shape deadlocks on the default path.
confirmed.fix: Derive the topic sides from send/reply (hosting = !reply, or send && !reply) so the documented two-party host publishes on "|offer", or update the header + MULTIPLAYER.md to state that send-only host mode is legacy/private-relay only.

confirmed.claim: rtc().stats().turn calls hasRelay() at call time rather than reporting the iceServers this connection was actually constructed with, so a credentials fetch landing after construction makes the lobby's failure copy give the wrong instruction.
confirmed.evidence: Line 515: `turn: hasRelay(),` inside stats(), and hasRelay() (401-406) recomputes iceServers({}) from the live fetchedIce/localStorage state, while the pc's config was fixed at line 419 (`new PC(cfg)`). lobby.js readyIce() races the prefetch with a 2500 ms cap (ICE_WAIT_MS) but the fetch itself has a 4000 ms budget (FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS, line 231), so a connection can be built STUN-only and fetchedIce land afterwards; failureMsg (lobby.js:320-326) then branches on st.turn and tells the player "A relay was offered and did not carry it" — the exact misleading diagnosis the lobby comment at 144-158 narrates as the historical bug.

confirmed.claim: codeReopen is never cleared by cancel()/teardown() or a failed handshake, so a stale room-code room silently reopens after a later, unrelated connection.

If the handshake then fails (waitForOpen timeout → dropPending, 388-397) or the player cancels (cancel(), 1584-1591 → teardown(), 259-272 — neither touches codeReopen), the value persists. The next successful connection — even from a plain link invite in a fresh hosting attempt — hits `if (codeReopen && transports.size < MAX_GUESTS)` in onConnected and calls codeHost({code: oldStaleCode, quiet:true}), reopening a room on a code the player believes is dead, with its onTick say() overwriting the status line with that old code.

confirmed.claim: The loopback comment says loss and reorder apply only to the "state" channel, but jitter is applied to every channel, so the reliable/ordered "event" channel can deliver out of order under jitter.

But enqueue() gates only loss on `channel === STATE` (104-106); line 110 computes `at = wire + latency + (jitter ? (rnd()*2-1)*jitter : 0)` for every message, and deliverTo() sorts by `(at, seq)` (122), so two EVENT messages whose jittered arrival times cross are emitted in reversed order — a scenario the comment says cannot happen and that real RTC's ordered channel never produces, breaking the substitutability the file insists on.
confirmed.fix: Apply the jitter term only when channel === STATE; give EVENT messages the fixed latency.
